Algebra I · Lesson 5.5

Word Problems with Systems

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Here the equations are yours to write. A story states its facts in plain English, and the two letters, what each one stands for, and one equation for each fact all have to be written down first. After that the system is an ordinary one and 5.2 or 5.3 finishes it. Try the next two stories before any of this has a name.

Problem
A ferry charges one fixed fare for a motorcycle and another for a car. The fares from 4 motorcycles and 3 cars come to 64 dollars, and the fares from 6 motorcycles and 7 cars come to 126 dollars. Enter the fare for one motorcycle, in dollars.
Show a hint
  • Two fares are unknown here, one for a motorcycle and one for a car. Name both, then write one equation for each of the two totals.
  • With mm dollars for a motorcycle and cc dollars for a car, 4m+3c=644m+3c=64 and 6m+7c=1266m+7c=126. No letter has coefficient 11, so isolating one brings fractions. Scale both equations and eliminate the 5.3 way instead.
Show the full solution
With mm dollars for a motorcycle and cc for a car, 4m+3c=644m+3c=64 and 6m+7c=1266m+7c=126. Tripling the first and doubling the second gives 12m+9c=19212m+9c=192 and 12m+14c=25212m+14c=252, and subtracting leaves 5c=605c=60, so c=12c=12, then 4m=64−36=284m=64−36=28 and m=7m=7​. Check, 6(7)+7(12)=42+84=1266(7)+7(12)=42+84=126. Neither total is made of one fare alone, so no single total gives a fare by itself, and the story needs two letters.
Problem
A photo lab made 143 prints on Tuesday, some small and some large. The number of small prints was 5 more than twice the number of large prints. Enter how many large prints the lab made that day.
Show a hint
  • Name both counts before anything else, LL for the large prints and SS for the small prints. Two separate facts are stated here, the total of 143 and the description of SS in terms of LL, so two equations come out of them.
  • With LL large prints and SS small prints the total is L+S=143L+S=143. Twice the large count is 2L2L, so the second sentence reads S=2L+5S=2L+5. Replace SS in the total.
Show the full solution
L+S=143L+S=143 and S=2L+5S=2L+5, so L+(2L+5)=143L+(2L+5)=143, 3L=1383L=138, and L=46L=46​, with S=97S=97. Check, 2(46)+5=972(46)+5=97 and 46+97=14346+97=143. Five more than twice LL is 2L+52L+5 and not 2(L+5)2(L+5), since only the large count is doubled.
Key idea
The two-variable routine. This is 4.5's routine with the count raised from one letter to two. Say what both letters stand for, units included. Translate each separate fact into its own equation, one equation per fact. Solve with 5.2 or 5.3, build the quantity the question names, then check the pair against the story. What is new is naming a second quantity, finding a second fact, and reading the closing sentence again at the end, since with two numbers in hand the one asked for is often neither of them.
Problem
A greenhouse bench holds shallow trays of 12 cells and deep trays of 20 cells, 37 trays and 588 cells in all. Enter how many of the trays are deep.
Show a hint
  • Name the two tray counts. The bench is counted twice, once in trays and once in cells, so there are two facts to translate.
  • With ss shallow trays and dd deep trays, s+d=37s+d=37 and 12s+20d=58812s+20d=588. Substitute s=37−ds=37−d.
Show the full solution
12(37−d)+20d=58812(37−d)+20d=588, so 444+8d=588444+8d=588, then 8d=1448d=144 and d=18d=18​. The other 19 trays are shallow, and 12(19)+20(18)=58812(19)+20(18)=588. Counting trays and counting cells are separate measurements, so the story needs two equations, not one.
Problem
A school stationery order was 52 items, all pens and markers. Pens cost 3 dollars each, markers cost 7 dollars each, and the whole order cost 264 dollars. Enter how many of the items were pens.
Show a hint
  • Write one equation for the 52 items and a second for the 264 dollars.
  • With pp pens and mm markers, p+m=52p+m=52 and 3p+7m=2643p+7m=264. Rewrite the first as p=52−mp=52−m and put that into the second.
Show the full solution
With pp pens and mm markers, p+m=52p+m=52 and 3p+7m=2643p+7m=264. Put p=52−mp=52−m into the cost equation to get 156+4m=264156+4m=264, so 4m=1084m=108 and m=27m=27. Then p=52−27=25p=52−27=25​. The count and the cost are two separate facts about the same order, so each one gets its own equation.
Key idea
One separate fact, one equation. A fact is separate when it can be checked on its own. Counting the trays and counting the cells are two different measurements of the same bench, so s+d=37s+d=37 and 12s+20d=58812s+20d=588 are two claims rather than one claim written twice. That is the test to run on a story before writing anything down. Translate the same fact twice, once in each of its two wordings, and the second equation is only a scaled copy of the first. Eliminating then gives 0=00=0, which is 5.3's case of infinitely many pairs.
Problem
A hardware bin holds 118 fasteners, each one a bolt or a screw. The number of bolts is 14 less than three times the number of screws. Enter how many bolts are in the bin.
Show a hint
  • Name both counts, ss for the screws and bb for the bolts. The total of 118 is one fact and the sentence comparing the two counts is the other.
  • Three times the screw count is 3s3s, and 14 less than that is 3s−143s−14, so b=3s−14b=3s−14. Put that into s+b=118s+b=118.
Show the full solution
With ss screws and bb bolts, s+b=118s+b=118 and b=3s−14b=3s−14. Substituting gives s+(3s−14)=118s+(3s−14)=118, so 4s=1324s=132 and s=33s=33, which makes b=3(33)−14=85b=3(33)−14=85​. Check, 33+85=11833+85=118. Fourteen less than 3s3s is 3s−143s−14 and not 14−3s14−3s, and the reversed version gives a negative bolt count.

Solving a system produces two numbers, and the question often asks for a third, the difference between them, the larger of the two, or a cost built from both. The work is the same either way. What changes is which number gets typed, and stopping at a letter's value is the most common way to work a story correctly and still answer it wrong.

Problem
A campsite charges one price per tent night and one price per cabin night, unchanged all season. Three tent nights and two cabin nights cost 214 dollars. Five tent nights and four cabin nights cost 396 dollars. Enter how much more one cabin night costs than one tent night, in dollars.
Show a hint
  • Name the two nightly prices and write one equation for each booking. Neither equation has a letter with coefficient 1, so elimination is the cheaper route.
  • With tt and cc in dollars per night, 3t+2c=2143t+2c=214 and 5t+4c=3965t+4c=396. Doubling the first equation matches the cc-columns at 4c4c. The closing sentence asks for a difference, not for either nightly price.
Show the full solution
Doubling 3t+2c=2143t+2c=214 gives 6t+4c=4286t+4c=428, and subtracting 5t+4c=3965t+4c=396 leaves t=32t=32. Then 96+2c=21496+2c=214 gives c=59c=59, and the ask is c−t=59−32=27c−t=59−32=27​. Check, 5(32)+4(59)=3965(32)+4(59)=396. Typing 5959 answers a question the problem did not ask, since 5959 is the cabin price and the story asked for the gap between the two prices.
Key idea
Answer the question that was asked. The two letters are yours to name and the question was fixed before you named them, so there is no reason the answer has to be one of them. Once the pair is found, read the closing sentence again and build the quantity it names, c−tc−t, the larger of the two, the cost of one of each. A pair found correctly and typed as the wrong quantity is marked exactly like a pair found wrong.
Problem
A bakery sold 141 loaves, sourdough and rye, with 27 fewer rye loaves than sourdough. Let ss be the number of sourdough loaves and rr the number of rye loaves. A student writes s+r=141s+r=141 and s=r−27s=r−27, solves that pair correctly, and both of the student's equations check against the pair that comes out. Fix the equation that is a wrong translation and enter the correct number of rye loaves.
Show a hint
  • The student's arithmetic is sound, so the error is in the translation. Solve the student's pair, then read the result against the sentence about 27 fewer rye loaves than sourdough.
  • 84 rye against 57 sourdough makes rye the larger count, so the minus sits on the wrong letter. The story says r=s−27r=s−27.
Show the full solution
The story makes rye the smaller count, so r=s−27r=s−27. Then s+(s−27)=141s+(s−27)=141, giving 2s=1682s=168 and s=84s=84, so r=57r=57​. The wrong pair and the right pair are the same two numbers swapped, and no algebraic check tells them apart. Only the English says which count is the larger one.
Key idea
Check the pair against the story. Substituting a solution into the equations you wrote always works, so that check cannot catch a bad translation. Read the two numbers back into the story's sentences one at a time instead. With two letters there is a second way to go wrong, which of the two quantities each letter stands for, and the pair (57,84)(57,84) satisfies s=r−27s=r−27 exactly while the English says rye is the smaller count. Only the story rejects it.

Prealgebra 7.3 gives distance as rate times time, d=rtd=rt. A boat moving with a current covers ground at its own still-water speed plus the current's speed, and moving against it at its own speed minus the current's speed. Both speeds are unknown, so name them bb and cc. Each trip is one fact, so a round trip is a two-fact story.

Problem
A river tour boat runs 90 km downstream in 3 hours, then the same 90 km back upstream in 5 hours. The current holds one steady speed all day, and the boat's speed in still water is the same on both legs. Enter that still-water speed, in km per hour.
Show a hint
  • Each leg has an actual speed you can work out right away, distance divided by time. That is 90÷390÷3 one way and 90÷590÷5 the other.
  • Call the boat's still-water speed bb and the current's speed cc. The current is with the boat downstream and against it upstream, so b+c=30b+c=30 and b−c=18b−c=18, and the cc-terms are already opposite.
Show the full solution
Let bb be the boat's speed in still water and cc the current's speed. Each leg's actual speed is distance over time, 90÷3=3090÷3=30 downstream and 90÷5=1890÷5=18 upstream, so b+c=30b+c=30 and b−c=18b−c=18. Adding gives 2b=482b=48, so b=24b=24​, with c=6c=6. The current is with the boat one way and against it the other, so the two cc-terms are opposite and one addition finishes the system.
Problem
A small plane covers 1400 km with a steady wind in 4 hours, then covers the same 1400 km back against that wind in 5 hours. The wind holds one steady speed and the plane's speed in still air is the same on both legs. Enter the wind's speed, in km per hour.
Show a hint
  • Two speeds are unknown here, the plane's speed in still air and the wind's speed, so give each one a letter. With the wind those two speeds add, and against the wind they subtract.
  • Each leg gives a ground speed, 1400÷4=3501400÷4=350 with the wind and 1400÷5=2801400÷5=280 against it, so p+w=350p+w=350 and p−w=280p−w=280. Subtracting the second equation from the first removes pp.
Show the full solution
The ground speeds are 1400÷4=3501400÷4=350 and 1400÷5=2801400÷5=280, so p+w=350p+w=350 and p−w=280p−w=280. Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 2w=702w=70, so w=35w=35​, with p=315p=315. Check, 1400÷350=41400÷350=4 and 1400÷280=51400÷280=5. The ask is the wind's speed, so 315315 is not the value to enter.
Fun fact
Around 800 CE Alcuin of York, a scholar at Charlemagne's court, compiled Propositiones ad Acuendos Juvenes, Problems to Sharpen the Young, fifty-three puzzles told as short stories about ferrymen, granaries and flocks.

Counts are not the only facts a story can state. A measured length is a fact too, and it translates the same way. Prealgebra 11.5 gives a rectangle's perimeter as 2L+2W2L+2W, so a stated perimeter is one equation, and any second length measured across the same rectangle is the other. Two measurements pin down both dimensions.

Problem
A rectangular garden bed is edged with 100 m of timber all the way around. A soaker hose runs along one full length and both widths, and it measures 64 m. Enter the length of the bed, in meters.
Show a hint
  • Name the length LL and the width WW, both in meters, and write one equation for the timber and one for the hose. The timber goes all the way around, so it uses each dimension twice.
  • The system is 2L+2W=1002L+2W=100 and L+2W=64L+2W=64. Both equations carry 2W2W, so subtracting one from the other clears WW in a single move.
Show the full solution
The timber gives 2L+2W=1002L+2W=100 and the hose gives L+2W=64L+2W=64. Both carry 2W2W, so subtracting the second from the first leaves L=36L=36​. Then 36+2W=6436+2W=64 gives W=14W=14. Check, 2(36)+2(14)=1002(36)+2(14)=100 and 36+28=6436+28=64. Each measured length in the story is its own equation, and two of them are enough to give both dimensions.

A two-digit number is not the sum of its digits and not their product. With tens digit tt and units digit uu the number is worth 10t+u10t+u, since a digit in the tens place is worth ten times its face value. Reversing the two digits gives 10u+t10u+t. Both are ordinary expressions in two letters, so a fact about either one is an equation.

Problem
The digits of a two-digit number add to 11, and reversing the digits gives a number 27 greater than the original. Enter the original number.
Show a hint
  • The two letters are the digits, not the number. Write the original as 10t+u10t+u and the reversed number as 10u+t10u+t.
  • (10u+t)−(10t+u)(10u+t)−(10t+u) collects to 9u−9t9u−9t, so the second fact is u−t=3u−t=3. Pair that with t+u=11t+u=11.
Show the full solution
The reversal fact is (10u+t)−(10t+u)=27(10u+t)−(10t+u)=27, which collects to 9u−9t=279u−9t=27, so u−t=3u−t=3. With t+u=11t+u=11, adding gives 2u=142u=14, so u=7u=7 and t=4t=4, and the number is 4747​. Solving gives the two digits, and the number still has to be rebuilt as 10t+u10t+u. Typing 44 or 77 answers a question the story did not ask.
Key idea
Naming the right two quantities is most of the work. Write both meanings down with units before anything else, the number of deep trays, the current's speed in kilometers per hour, the tens digit. Name the wrong two and the system is still solvable, the arithmetic is still clean, and the pair at the end answers a different question. No later step can undo that. The choice is free, so pick the two quantities the story's facts are about, since each fact can then be translated word for word.
Problem
A repair counter charges one fixed price to reseal a window and one to rehang a door. One week it resealed 12 windows and rehung 7 doors for 438 dollars. The next week it resealed 9 windows and rehung 11 doors for 432 dollars. Enter the total cost of one reseal and one rehang, in dollars.
Show a hint
  • The counts of jobs are given, so the two unknowns are the price of a reseal and the price of a rehang. Name those two prices and write one equation for each week's takings.
  • The system is 12w+7d=43812w+7d=438 and 9w+11d=4329w+11d=432. Neither letter has coefficient 11, so eliminate one by scaling. The reseal coefficients 1212 and 99 both divide 3636.
Show the full solution
With ww the price of a reseal and dd the price of a rehang, the two facts are 12w+7d=43812w+7d=438 and 9w+11d=4329w+11d=432. Scaling the first by 33 and the second by 44 gives 36w+21d=131436w+21d=1314 and 36w+44d=172836w+44d=1728, and subtracting leaves 23d=41423d=414, so d=18d=18. Then 12w+126=43812w+126=438 gives w=26w=26, so w+d=44w+d=44​. Neither price on its own is the answer, since the question asks for the sum.

Every story here named two quantities and stated two facts, and each system was written one sentence at a time. Some stories name three, a triangle's three angles or three prices on one receipt. Three quantities, three facts. Lesson 5.6, Three or More Variables, raises the count, and elimination still applies, clearing one letter at a time.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A bike shop charges one fixed price to true a wheel and one fixed price to replace a brake pad. Two wheel truings and three pad replacements cost 61 dollars, and two truings and one pad replacement cost 39 dollars. Enter the price of one wheel truing, in dollars.
Show the solution
With tt the price of one truing and pp the price of one pad replacement, 2t+3p=612t+3p=61 and 2t+p=392t+p=39. Subtracting the second from the first leaves 2p=222p=22, so p=11p=11, and then 2t+11=392t+11=39 gives 2t=282t=28 and t=14t=14​. Both visits hold the same two truings, so the 22 dollar gap is the cost of two pad replacements.
Practice
A jar holds 45 marbles, each one red or blue. Each red marble weighs 6 grams, each blue marble weighs 4 grams, and the marbles weigh 232 grams in all. Enter how many of the marbles are red.
Show the solution
With rr red marbles and bb blue, r+b=45r+b=45 and 6r+4b=2326r+4b=232. Put 45−r45−r in for bb to get 6r+4(45−r)=2326r+4(45−r)=232, so 2r+180=2322r+180=232 and r=26r=26​. The other 19 marbles are blue, and 26⋅6+19⋅4=23226⋅6+19⋅4=232 grams.
Practice
A vending machine holds 30 bars, all of them granola bars or protein bars. Granola bars sell for 2 dollars each and protein bars sell for 3 dollars each, and the 30 bars are worth 79 dollars in all. Enter how many of the bars are protein bars.
Show the solution
With gg granola bars and pp protein bars, g+p=30g+p=30 and 2g+3p=792g+3p=79. Substitute g=30−pg=30−p into the second equation. Then 2(30−p)+3p=792(30−p)+3p=79, so 60+p=7960+p=79 and p=19p=19​. The other 11 bars are granola, and 2⋅11+3⋅19=792⋅11+3⋅19=79.
Practice
A workshop packs hinges into small crates and large crates, each crate size holding a fixed number of hinges. One shipment of 4 small crates and 3 large crates holds 117 hinges. Another shipment of 2 small crates and 5 large crates holds 139 hinges. Enter how many hinges one large crate holds.
Show the solution
Let xx be the hinges in a small crate and yy the hinges in a large crate. The first shipment gives 4x+3y=1174x+3y=117 and the second gives 2x+5y=1392x+5y=139. Doubling the second gives 4x+10y=2784x+10y=278, and subtracting the first leaves 7y=1617y=161, so y=23y=23​. A small crate holds 1212 hinges, and 4(12)+3(23)=1174(12)+3(23)=117 matches the first shipment.
Practice
A print shop charges the same price for every poster and the same price for every sticker. One order of 4 posters and 3 stickers cost 41 dollars. Another order of 2 posters and 7 stickers cost 37 dollars. Enter the price of one poster, in dollars.
Show the solution
With pp dollars for a poster and ss dollars for a sticker, the two orders read 4p+3s=414p+3s=41 and 2p+7s=372p+7s=37. Doubling the second gives 4p+14s=744p+14s=74, and subtracting the first leaves 11s=3311s=33, so s=3s=3 and 4p=41−9=324p=41−9=32, which makes p=8p=8​. The prices fit the story, 4 posters and 3 stickers cost 32+9=4132+9=41 dollars and 2 posters and 7 stickers cost 16+21=3716+21=37 dollars.
Practice
Every crate of apples weighs the same and every crate of pears weighs the same. Three crates of apples and two crates of pears weigh 63 kg together, and one crate of apples weighs 6 kg more than one crate of pears. Enter the weight of one crate of pears, in kilograms.
Show the solution
Let aa be the weight of one crate of apples in kilograms and pp the weight of one crate of pears. Then 3a+2p=633a+2p=63 and a=p+6a=p+6, so 3(p+6)+2p=633(p+6)+2p=63, giving 5p+18=635p+18=63 and p=9p=9​. Check, a=15a=15 and 3(15)+2(9)=633(15)+2(9)=63. The 3 and the 2 are crate counts and the letters are weights, so 3a3a is the weight of all three apple crates.
Practice
A nursery's fern count is 8 less than three times its palm count, and the two counts add to 140. Enter how many palms the nursery has.
Show the solution
With pp palms and ff ferns, f=3p−8f=3p−8 and f+p=140f+p=140, so (3p−8)+p=140(3p−8)+p=140, giving 4p=1484p=148 and p=37p=37​. Check, f=103f=103, 103+37=140103+37=140 and 3(37)−8=1033(37)−8=103. Reversing the order to f=8−3pf=8−3p gives p=−66p=−66, a negative palm count, so the order the sentence names is what the translation has to keep.
Practice
A stall sold 56 cups of cider. Small cups cost 3 dollars each and large cups cost 5 dollars each, and the stall took in 204 dollars from those 56 cups. Enter how many more small cups than large cups it sold.
Show the solution
With ss small cups and LL large, s+L=56s+L=56 and 3s+5L=2043s+5L=204. Substituting s=56−Ls=56−L gives 3(56−L)+5L=2043(56−L)+5L=204, so 168+2L=204168+2L=204, L=18L=18, and s=38s=38. The ask is s−L=38−18=20s−L=38−18=20​. The question asks for the difference, not for either count, so the subtraction at the end is easy to skip.
Practice
A ranger counted deer and elk on one range. Three times the deer count is 40 more than the elk count, and the elk count is 8 less than twice the deer count. Enter how many elk the ranger counted.
Show the solution
With dd deer and ee elk, 3d=e+403d=e+40 and e=2d−8e=2d−8. Substituting gives 3d=(2d−8)+403d=(2d−8)+40, so d=32d=32, and then e=2(32)−8=56e=2(32)−8=56​. Check, 3(32)=963(32)=96 and 56+40=9656+40=96. A story can pin a pair down with two comparisons and no total at all.
Practice
An airport walkway is 96 m long. Walking along it in the direction it moves, a traveler covers the 96 m in 24 seconds. Walking back along it against its direction, at the same walking speed, the traveler covers the same 96 m in 48 seconds. Enter that walking speed in meters per second, the speed the traveler would walk on a floor that does not move.
Show the solution
The two ground speeds are 96÷24=496÷24=4 and 96÷48=296÷48=2. With ww the walking speed and mm the walkway's speed, w+m=4w+m=4 and w−m=2w−m=2. Adding the two gives 2w=62w=6, so w=3w=3​. Then m=1m=1, which fits both times. With only one trip you would know just w+mw+m, so the second trip is what separates the two speeds.
Practice
A rectangular courtyard has a perimeter of 84 m, and its length is 4 m more than its width. Enter its area, in square meters.
Show the solution
With LL the length and WW the width, 2L+2W=842L+2W=84 and L=W+4L=W+4. Dividing the first by 22 gives L+W=42L+W=42, and substituting L=W+4L=W+4 gives 2W+4=422W+4=42, so W=19W=19 and L=23L=23. The area is 23×19=43723×19=437​ square meters. Neither letter is the answer on its own, since the question asks for the product of the two sides.
Practice
Plum boxes sell for 4 dollars and fig boxes sell for 7 dollars. A stall sold 11 more plum boxes than fig boxes and took in 187 dollars from those boxes. Let pp be the number of plum boxes and ff the number of fig boxes. Nia writes f=p+11f=p+11 and 4p+7f=1874p+7f=187, solves that pair correctly, and gets p=10p=10 and f=21f=21. Her values satisfy both equations she wrote. Fix the wrong translation and enter the correct number of fig boxes.
Show the solution
The stall sold 11 more plum boxes than fig boxes, so the first equation should read p=f+11p=f+11. Then 4(f+11)+7f=1874(f+11)+7f=187 gives 11f+44=18711f+44=187, so 11f=14311f=143 and f=13f=13​. Then p=24p=24, and 4(24)+7(13)=96+91=1874(24)+7(13)=96+91=187. Nia's two values are whole numbers and they fit both of the equations she wrote, so only a reread of the English sentence catches the error.
Practice
An isosceles triangle has a perimeter of 95 cm, and each of its two equal sides is 5 cm shorter than twice the base. Enter the length of the base, in centimeters.
Show the solution
With bb the base and ss one equal side, 2s+b=952s+b=95 and s=2b−5s=2b−5. Substituting gives 2(2b−5)+b=952(2b−5)+b=95, so 5b−10=955b−10=95 and b=21b=21​. Check against the story, s=2(21)−5=37s=2(21)−5=37 and 2(37)+21=952(37)+21=95. The perimeter counts the equal side twice, so the first equation is 2s+b2s+b and not s+bs+b.
Practice
A two-digit number is 7 times the sum of its digits, and reversing its digits gives a number 18 less than the original. Enter the original number.
Show the solution
With tt the tens digit and uu the units digit, the number is 10t+u10t+u and its reversal is 10u+t10u+t. The first fact reads 10t+u=7(t+u)10t+u=7(t+u), which simplifies to 3t=6u3t=6u, so t=2ut=2u. The second reads 10u+t=10t+u−1810u+t=10t+u−18, which simplifies to t−u=2t−u=2. Then 2u−u=22u−u=2 makes u=2u=2 and t=4t=4, so the number is 4242​. Both facts hold for 42, since 7(4+2)=427(4+2)=42 and 24=42−1824=42−18.
Practice
A canteen charges the same price for every roll and the same price for every bowl of soup. Three rolls and two bowls of soup cost 37 dollars, and five rolls and three bowls of soup cost 59 dollars. Enter the cost of four rolls and three bowls of soup, in dollars.
Show the solution
With rr the price of a roll and ss the price of a bowl of soup, 3r+2s=373r+2s=37 and 5r+3s=595r+3s=59. Tripling the first gives 9r+6s=1119r+6s=111 and doubling the second gives 10r+6s=11810r+6s=118, so subtracting leaves r=7r=7, and 21+2s=3721+2s=37 gives s=8s=8. Four rolls and three bowls of soup cost 28+24=5228+24=52​ dollars. Neither price is the answer, and the closing sentence names a third amount built from both.
Practice
Two trains leave stations 468 km apart at the same moment and travel toward each other at steady speeds, meeting 3 hours later. One train is 14 km per hour faster than the other. Enter how far the faster train traveled, in kilometers.
Show the solution
With xx the slower rate and yy the faster, in km per hour, the two distances add to 468, so 3x+3y=4683x+3y=468 and x+y=156x+y=156. The second fact is y=x+14y=x+14, so 2x+14=1562x+14=156, x=71x=71, and y=85y=85. The faster train travels 3(85)=2553(85)=255​ km. The letters stand for rates and the question asks for a distance, so multiply the faster rate by the 3 hours.
Practice
A ticket window sells lawn seats at 18 dollars and pavilion seats at 32 dollars. One night it sold 11 fewer pavilion seats than lawn seats and took in 1898 dollars. Enter how much more money came from pavilion seats than from lawn seats, in dollars.
Show the solution
With LL lawn seats and PP pavilion seats, P=L−11P=L−11 and 18L+32P=189818L+32P=1898, so 18L+32(L−11)=189818L+32(L−11)=1898, giving 50L=225050L=2250 and L=45L=45, with P=34P=34. Pavilion money is 32(34)=108832(34)=1088 and lawn money is 18(45)=81018(45)=810, so the difference is 278278​ dollars. Neither 45 nor 34 is the answer, since each count still has to be multiplied by its own price before the subtraction.
